title: Private/VPC deployment: networking & air-gapped upgrade acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha R. Cohen
description: High-level product requirements and concrete acceptance criteria for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments focusing on networking constraints, upgrade mechanics, and air-gapped environments. This document captures the scope, non-goals, design constraints, and testable exit conditions for the upcoming private deployment release (release-private-2026.04). It is intended for PM, Eng, Security, and Solutions teams to align on what we ship and how customers will validate upgrades in restricted networks.
requirements: R1: Support offline (air-gapped) upgrade packages that can be delivered via customer-approved media (tarball/OCI archive) and applied without egress to Redwood control plane.
R2: Allow operator-driven upgrade with optional proxy/HTTP-mirror support for customers with restricted egress through corporate proxies or whitelisted registries.
R3: Define a canonical signed manifest format for release artifacts (SHA256 checksums + detached signature) and tooling to verify signatures locally against customer-managed keys.
R4: Provide an operator CLI 'redwood-upgrade' with idempotent apply, preflight checks, and dry-run modes; CLI must run without internet access once artifacts are present.
R5: Network requirements doc: minimal inbound/outbound rules, ports, and recommended subnet & routing topologies for VPC and on-prem installs (including NAT, private link, and VPN cases).
R6: Upgrade orchestration must support rolling upgrades across nodes with a configurable max concurrency (default=1 node at a time) and health-check gating to prevent rollout on unhealthy clusters.
R7: Provide instrumentation and local bundle of upgrade health checks (smoke tests) that validate API readiness, KV cache warmup, model load success, and routing table integrity post-upgrade.
R8: Offer a documented remediation path and single-command rollback that reverts service binaries and runtime state when smoke tests indicate failure.

R9: Telemetry-for-audit: produce an audit artifact for each upgrade containing pre/post manifests, node-by-node status, timestamps, operator identity (if available), and checksums; artifact must be exportable for customer retention.
R10: Ensure optional integration points for KMS/HSM: artifact verification can use customer KMS public keys and optional hardware-backed verification during upgrade preflight.
R11: Minimal control-plane connectivity mode: support upgrades when control plane access is intentionally disabled, by providing fully self-contained upgrade bundles and a documented operator flow.
R12: Document required proxy configuration patterns for registries and package mirrors (including example apt/yum/docker registries and environment variables).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Offline bundle installation: Using only a provided release bundle (no outbound network), an operator can perform a full upgrade on a 3-node evaluation cluster and end-to-end smoke tests pass within 30 minutes.

AC2: Signed manifest verification: The operator CLI rejects any bundle whose manifest checksum or signature does not validate against the configured public key; error messages must be actionable and include the failing file and expected checksum.

AC3: Rolling upgrade safety: With default concurrency=1, no more than one serving process is restarted at a time. During rollout the cluster API remains available and <1% of successful requests experience 5xx errors during a well-formed upgrade of the evaluation cluster.

AC4: Proxy/mirror compatibility: In a customer mirror environment (HTTP proxy requiring auth), the CLI can be configured to use the mirror and complete an upgrade end-to-end; documentation contains an example for at least Docker registry and Debian package mirror setups.
AC5: Health-check gating: The orchestrator will automatically pause rollout on a node failing the smoke tests and surface a clear remediation reason in the CLI output and upgrade artifact.

AC6: Rollback: After intentionally introducing a failing config change in a staged upgrade, invoking the documented rollback command restores the previous service version and all smoke tests return to 'pass' within a defined RTO (default 15 minutes for evaluation cluster).

AC7: Audit artifact: For each upgrade run, an artifact is produced and can be exported to a local path; the artifact contains timestamps, operator identity, checksums, node results and an overall pass/fail flag.

AC8: Documentation completeness: Install & upgrade runbook includes step-by-step offline upgrade, proxy configuration examples, troubleshooting steps for common network failures (DNS, MTU, proxy auth), and a short playbook for customer support to request additional artifacts.
AC9: Security verification: Security team verifies the manifest/signature approach and KMS integration. Security review sign-off recorded in the ticket before release (security_review_required=true).

AC10: Compatibility: The upgrade flow is tested against both Dedicated-like GPU nodes and CPU-only control-plane nodes; any platform-specific caveats are documented and surfaced during preflight checks.

AC11: Non-regression on observability: After upgrade, per-route latency/cost dashboards and token-level tracing remain available to the tenant UI (or local artifacts if UI is disabled); missing telemetry generates a warning in the artifact.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Engineering validation on internal air-gapped lab (2 weeks) with 3-node and 6-node clusters. Phase 2: Early access with 3 pilot customers (solutions-runbook + runbook rehearsal). Phase 3: GA documentation + release. Each phase includes a dry-run and a signed-manifest policy review.
downgrade_and_rollback: Rollback is implemented as a two-step operation: 1) orchestrator stops new binaries and re-deploys previous release artifacts; 2) operator triggers post-rollback smoke tests. Rollback must be idempotent and safe when re-run. Rollback instructions include steps to restore cached models if the new release changed on-disk formats.
test_plan: Automated CI: unit tests for manifest parsing, signature verification, and preflight checks. Integration: internal airgap lab runs nightly upgrade/downgrade permutations. Manual: customer playbook walkthroughs with Solutions engineers for pilot customers. Test matrix included: proxy/no-proxy, NAT-only, VPN (split-tunnel), and completely offline.
notes:
- Keep default concurrency conservative; customer can opt-in for faster parallelism.
- Consider adding a 'pre-warm' option to allocate models to GPUs ahead of draining to reduce post-upgrade latency spikes.
- Coordinate with Support to prepare artifact request template for troubleshooting.
- This ticket intentionally excludes live database schema migrations; those will be separate PRDs.
